title: Take the tour
note: The guided tour. Take the tour with no path named walks the fence, the café and the city. Each of those tracks opens on a story. The tour only opens screens and points at controls. It never changes a record.

steps.title: A fence for the back yard
steps.copy_note: This track makes its own application, so it needs no copy.
steps.caption: We are here because a resident at 400 Lantern Row wants a fence for the back yard. The case starts on Apply, before a form is filled, because the permit and the documents are not known yet.

steps.title: Ask which permit a fence needs
steps.muse_line: Muse, in the help assistant, names the fence permit, the 4 ft front yard limit and the documents.
steps.caption: We are here because the resident does not yet know which permit a back yard fence needs. Press Ask.

steps.title: Apply for a permit
steps.caption: We are here because the City asks only the questions this fence project needs. Press Residential deck or fence.

steps.title: Check the application before it is sent
steps.muse_line: Muse gives feedback on Check my application before the application is sent.

fields.project_description: A 4 ft cedar fence in the back yard.

file__site_plan.name: site-plan.txt
file__site_plan.text: Site plan: 4 ft fence in the back yard at 400 Lantern Row.

steps.caption: We are here because the resident should see what must change before the City does. Press Fill in the story’s answers, then Check my application. Try 6 ft in the front yard to see the check catch it.

steps.title: Let the agent route the application
steps.muse_line: Muse reads the documents on intake as a recorded Muse run (replay), and a person still decides.
steps.caption: We are here because the new application has to be read and sent to the right queue. Document reading is a recorded Muse run (replay). Press Wake agent.

steps.title: Track the application
steps.caption: We are here because the resident needs to see what the City has recorded so far. Open the application in the list.

steps.title: Read the messages from the City
steps.caption: We are here because the applicant is told of each decision. Open the application and read Messages from the City. The City would also send this by email. The demonstration sends no email.

steps.title: A café that has been waiting
steps.copy_note: Start fresh: get your own copy of the café case, so other visitors’ changes don’t get in your way.
steps.caption: We are here because Cedarline Coffee cannot open until its permit is issued. Start fresh: get your own copy of the café case, so other visitors’ changes don’t get in your way.

steps.title: Match the café to its owner
steps.copy_note: Start fresh: get your own copy of the café case, so other visitors’ changes don’t get in your way.
steps.muse_line: Explain with Muse rewrites the reason in plain words, and a person records the decision.
steps.caption: We are here because the owner is three records until a steward decides they are one. The Agent Operator or the Data Steward wakes the Steward assistant. Press Wake, or Wake agent, then Prepare recommendations.

steps.title: Let the agent route the case
steps.muse_line: Muse reads the documents on intake as a recorded Muse run (replay), and a person still decides.
steps.caption: We are here because the café case has to reach a reviewer, and only a person may approve it. Document reading is a recorded Muse run (replay). Press Wake agent.

steps.title: Run the checks and approve the case
steps.caption: We are here because a person decides the case, and Data follow-up does not block it. Press Run application checks or Run checks again. The applicant is told by email at this point. The demonstration sends no email.

steps.title: Apply the café’s payment
steps.caption: We are here because the café paid its 150.00 fee when it applied, but the payment came in under its old finance account, so nobody could match it to the case. Press Assess application, Confirm allocation and Reconcile assessment.

steps.title: Issue the permit
steps.caption: We are here because deciding and issuing are separate, and the payer link and the fee still block issuing until both are clear. Press Issue permit. The applicant is told by email at this point. The demonstration sends no email.

steps.title: Find it as a resident
steps.caption: We are here because a resident should find the permit without a homeowner’s name, the documents or the fees. Search the public record.

steps.title: Should the City change the fee or the process?
steps.copy_note: This track does not change any case, so it needs no copy.
steps.caption: We are here because cafés like Cedarline waited weeks for a permit. Should the City change the commercial fee, or the process? Start with the counts, because that is where the wait shows up.

steps.title: See where the weeks went
steps.caption: We are here because the weeks cafés waited should show up in the counts. Open the City view and read the counts, the map and the definition beside each figure for commercial cases.

steps.title: Follow where the café’s time went
steps.caption: We are here because the counts raise where the café’s weeks went. Choose Recorded permit decision, press Apply filters, then press View details.

steps.title: Ask Muse what the pattern is
steps.muse_line: Muse summarises the pattern in the policy briefing, and it decides nothing.
steps.caption: We are here because the record shows a pattern and Muse should summarise it before any rule changes. Open More details and press Ask Muse to propose.

steps.title: Try the fee change
steps.muse_line: Muse writes the policy briefing for the what-if, and the run decides nothing.
steps.caption: We are here because the question is whether a fee change would shorten the wait. Press Create a what-if and see the effect before any rule changes.

steps.title: Leave the change for a person
steps.caption: We are here because the fee question is answered only when a person approves the change. A person must approve and publish it.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.caption: We are here because the question has an answer only when a person approves it. The video, the permit life cycle and Help and documentation are there when you want them.

steps.title: Watch the video
steps.caption: We are here because the video shows the same journey before you walk it. Press play on the video.

steps.title: Read the permit life cycle
steps.caption: We are here because each move names who makes it, and an agent only routes. Read the main path.

steps.title: See what the City plans next
steps.caption: We are here because the help hub holds the guides and the plan for what is not built yet. Open the help cards.
